title: Why your ears ring after a loud concert 🔊
subject: ear
description:
How long did your ears ring after your loudest concert? 👇

The ringing after a loud show is a sign that the sensory hair cells in your inner ear were overworked. In a 2009 study, Sharon Kujawa and Charles Liberman of Harvard Medical School exposed mice to 2 hours of 100-decibel noise: their hearing thresholds recovered completely, yet up to about half of the nerve connections in the most affected part of the cochlea were permanently lost. NIOSH's workplace limit allows 100 dBA for only 15 minutes a day.

Sources: Kujawa & Liberman, "Adding insult to injury: cochlear nerve degeneration after 'temporary' noise-induced hearing loss," Journal of Neuroscience (2009); NIH NIDCD, "How does loud noise cause hearing loss?"; CDC/NIOSH, "Understand Noise Exposure"; Cleveland Clinic, "Ears ringing from a loud concert? Why that's not a good sign".

scenes.text: Your ears ring after a concert. Something in there got hurt.
Deep in each ear, tiny hair cells turn sound into nerve signals. Loud music batters them.
A day later the ringing fades, and your hearing tests normal.
In 2009, Harvard researchers Sharon Kujawa and Charles Liberman blasted mice with 2 hours of 100-decibel noise. Their hearing recovered.
Up to half the nerve connections in the hardest-hit area never came back.
U.S. workplace limits allow 100 decibels for 15 minutes. Concerts last hours.
